new_query: For two disjoint ranking claims on one shared path, what is the smallest adjacent-position budget that admits their conjunction, and how far can even ALL reanchored independent-box feasibility answers underestimate that necessary budget?
analytic_plan: For deficits a=l_p-u_q and b=l_r-u_s, own distances d1=|j_p-j_q|,d2=|j_r-j_s|, cross distance c=|j_p-j_s|+|j_r-j_q|, define delta_pair=max(0,a/d1,b/d2). The exact joint radius is delta_joint=max(delta_pair,(a+b)/c). Every real-anchor box admits the conjunction as soon as delta>=delta_pair, because disjoint interval comparisons are independent. Conversely the supremum over anchors of the individual-box feasibility radius equals delta_pair, so even querying every anchor cannot improve that lower bound. The continuous discrepancy window is [delta_pair,delta_joint), nonempty iff delta_joint>delta_pair. Prove these claims before computing new outcomes.
